evidence.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

value.rationale: The affirmative conditions match in both directions: licensed-corporation status, the three option types, non-central clearing, the inclusive 2026-01-04 threshold, and continued exemption force. However, the lowering also places their entire conjunction in executable scope. The original expressly defines false as failure of any stated condition; the lowering instead returns OUT_OF_SCOPE for those cases. For example, a transaction dated 2026-01-03 with all other conditions true yields false originally but OUT_OF_SCOPE after lowering. This changes the declared Boolean meaning. The supplied source supports the announced Hong Kong exemption; overseas provisions are explanatory background, and the pending Code amendment is not stated as an additional prerequisite. Neither version implements that amendment's status as a predicate.
uncertainty: The supplied classifications require external judgment; their correctness and the absence of a later modifying notice are not established here.
Referenced dependencies are unavailable in the supplied packet, so their contents and subsequent legal developments cannot be verified.

Both versions inherit ambiguity between transaction date and assessment date; the source announces when the exemption operates without expressly restricting coverage to transactions entered into after that date.
The start date is described as fixed but represented as a supplied fact; the backtranslation does not establish runtime enforcement of its declared value.
